time_period_note.default_value: 'Multi-year avg period as TEXT; not FK to Dim_Time - see PBCR publication'

cancer_type_note.default_value: 'UNIDENTIFIED - Dataset 5.docx does not state cancer type; scale (~77K national) suggests single-site (possibly ovarian); NOT all-cancer total'

state_incidence_outliers_2022.justification: Epidemiologically genuine high-population states (Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, West Bengal, Bihar, Tamil Nadu). Not data entry errors.

incompatible_units_safeguards.rule: Never sum counts and rates directly.
Percentages; evaluate with median or weighted average, not unweighted sum.
Ratio of deaths to incidence in single unidentified cancer cohort; not survival percentage.

regression.candidate_task: State-level cancer incidence trend & forecast evaluation
regression.available_observations: 37 states x 7 time points (259 records in Fact_State_Surveillance)
regression.data_limitations: 2019-2022 are model estimates; 2026-2045 are exponential forecasts. True ground-truth annual censuses do not exist for all 37 states.
regression.justification: FEASIBLE as an econometric trend regression comparing Linear Regression vs Ridge vs Polynomial on state historical baseline to validate forecast trajectories. Must document that targets are model estimates.

decision_tree.candidate_task: State cancer burden categorization (Low, Moderate, High, Severe)
decision_tree.target_variable: burden_tier (discretized by quartiles of 2022 incidence: Q1 < 5,800, Q2 5,800-24,000, Q3 24,000-72,000, Q4 > 72,000)
decision_tree.data_limitations: Small sample size (N=37). Risk of overfitting if tree depth > 3. Leave-One-Out or Stratified K-Fold (k=4) required.
decision_tree.justification: FEASIBLE with strict depth control (max_depth=3) and transparent quartile thresholds. Report confusion matrix, precision, recall.

naive_bayes.candidate_task: Probabilistic classification of cancer sites by primary risk attribution (Tobacco-Associated vs Non-Tobacco)
naive_bayes.available_observations: 76 cancer sites in Dim_Cancer_Site or 28 registries in Fact_PBCR_Surveillance
naive_bayes.data_limitations: Aggregated site statistics, not individual patient histories. GaussianNB or CategoricalNB appropriate.
naive_bayes.justification: FEASIBLE for classifying site tobacco association based on epidemiological rate profiles. Document that this classifies cancer anatomical types, not individual patients.

kmeans_clustering.candidate_task: Multivariate epidemiological profiling of 37 Indian States/UTs
kmeans_clustering.data_limitations: Outliers (UP, MH) skew unscaled data; StandardScaler mandatory. Optimal k evaluated via Silhouette Analysis and Elbow Method (k=3 to 5).
kmeans_clustering.justification: HIGHLY FEASIBLE and clinically meaningful for identifying homogeneous healthcare burden clusters.

hierarchical_clustering.candidate_task: Agglomerative hierarchical clustering with Dendrogram across 37 States and 32 Registries
hierarchical_clustering.available_observations: 37 states (state surveillance panel) and 28 registries (PBCR tobacco & rate vectors)
features: standardized incidence, growth rates, and regional vectors
hierarchical_clustering.justification: HIGHLY FEASIBLE. Produces a clear, readable dendrogram illustrating state and regional epidemiological clusters without overwhelming label clutter.

apriori_association_mining.candidate_task: Market-Basket / Co-occurrence Mining of High-Risk Cancer Epidemiological Attributes
apriori_association_mining.available_observations: 37 states or 76 sites discretized into categorical itemsets
apriori_association_mining.transaction_definition: States represented as baskets of categorical healthcare attributes (e.g., {'High_Incidence', 'High_Observed_Growth', 'High_Mortality_Ratio', 'Region_NorthEast', 'High_Tobacco_Burden'})
apriori_association_mining.data_limitations: Must discretize continuous metrics using statistically defensible quartile/median thresholds. Never fabricate fake transactions.
apriori_association_mining.justification: FEASIBLE under defensible quantile discretization. Report Support, Confidence, and Lift.
